data.paper_title: Profitability of Momentum Strategies: An Evaluation of Alternative Explanations
data.selected_experiment: Table 1, decile momentum portfolios (6-month ranking, 6-month holding) of NYSE/AMEX stocks, 1965-1989, 1990-1997 and 1965-1997

economic_rationale.value: Momentum profits are attributed to investors' underreaction to information (or delayed overreaction) rather than to cross-sectional variation in expected returns; past winners keep outperforming past losers over the following months.

evidence.quote: The behavioral models specify that the holding period returns arise because of a delayed overreaction to information that push the prices of winners (losers) above (below) their long-term values.

universe_and_filters.value: All NYSE/AMEX stocks; NASDAQ stocks excluded; stocks priced below $5 at the beginning of the holding period excluded

evidence.quote: We follow JT and include all NYSE/AMEX stocks and exclude NASDAQ stocks.

At the end of each month we rank the stocks in the sample based on their past six-month returns (month —5 to month 0) and then group the stocks into ten equally weighted portfolios based on these ranks.

evidence.quote: P1 is the equal-weighted portfolio of ten percent of the stocks with the highest six-month lagged returns, P2 is the equal-weighted portfolio of the ten percent of the stocks with the next highest returns and so on.

expected_sign_evidence.quote: The table reveals a monotonic relation between returns and momentum ranks over the 1965 to 1989 sample period, confirming the results in JT.
